title: Pagination, Filtering & Idempotency
objectives: Choose cursor over offset pagination for large tables
Design idempotent POST handling with an Idempotency-Key

examples.name: cursor.rs

exercise.prompt: Simulate idempotency: process POST /charge with Idempotency-Key values ["k1", "k1", "k2"] against a store; the second k1 must return the first result without charging again. Print attempts and charges.
hints: The key maps to the FIRST response; repeats never re-execute the operation.
charges increments only on a fresh key.

questions.prompt: Cursor pagination beats offset on deep pages because…
options: the DB starts at the keyset instead of scanning skipped rows
questions.explanation: OFFSET must walk all skipped rows; keyset seeks directly — constant cost per page.

options: duplicate side effects when the same request is retried
questions.explanation: Retries and network duplicates are inevitable; the key makes replay safe.
